facts.fact: Villa Vailima, the house Stevenson built and lived in during the last years of his life, is now a museum with items from the house or equivalents; about 5 km south of Apia
Stevenson bought 314 acres in 1890 and completed the villa in 1891; the museum shows a curated version of the residence as he lived in it
Entry listed as $15 (Wikivoyage; currency assumed WST, unverified; one other listing says USD 15-20)
Stevenson wrote 'The Bottle Imp' here for Samoans; its Samoan translation was the first non-Bible literature in Samoan

facts.fact: Catholic cathedral in Apia, one of the town's larger buildings, set apart by its cupolas and ornaments
Finished in the mid-19th century, badly damaged in the 2009 earthquake, reopened after renovation and extension in 2014
No admission fee mentioned by sources; free is an assumption, unverified

piula-cave-pool.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: OSM tourism=attraction 'Piula Cave Pool'; moved 54 m from placement point

facts.fact: Natural freshwater pool by the sea beneath the Methodist chapel at Piula, Lufilufi, 26 km east of Apia
Entered through the painted stone wall of Piula Theological College, steps lead down to the pool
Spring-fed pool for swimming and exploring caves; closed Sundays; 5 per person (tala assumed) plus 10 to drive down

facts.fact: Island in the Apolima Strait 3.4 km off Upolu's western tip; about a 20-minute boat trip
No cars or roads; a footpath follows the coast; dogs and horses banned
Four villages (889 people, 2006), beach fale accommodation, a prehistoric mound

facts.fact: Mount Matavanu is an active volcano on Savai'i formed by the 1905 eruption; lava flows covered much of Gaga'emauga and forced villages to relocate
Eruptions ran 1905-1911; recognised as an IUGS Geological Heritage Site in November 2022
Reached by a roughly three-hour walk from Paia village; the lava fields look like a barren moonscape
A local guide and caretaker fee are reported; round trip 3-6 hours
